body.p: Upon entry of this amendment, claims 1, 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23, 25-28, and 74-76 are pending. Claims 1, 8, and 23, are amended, claim 11 is in the original form, claims 4-7, 10, 12- 14, 16, 25-28, and 74-75 have been previously presented, claim 24 has been canceled, and claim 76 is added. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the application as filed, including at least in paragraphs [0098]-[0101] and the originally-filed claims. No new matter is added by this amendment. This Amendment is being made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and does not constitute an acquiescence to any prior art or rejections identified by the Office.

Claims 1, 4-8, 10-14, 16, and 23-28, and 74-75 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as allegedly being rendered obvious by US 2012/0265037 to Bohm et al. ("Bohm") in view of US 2011/0021889 to Hoss et al. ("Hoss") and in further view of US 2007/0038044 to Dobbles et al. ("Dobbles"). Office Action at 2. Although Applicant does not necessarily agree with the Office, to expedite allowance of this Application, Applicant has made clarifying amendments to claims 1, 8, and 23 to further clarify the distinction between the claims and the cited art.
Independent claim 1 of this Application, as amended, recites:
1. A method of determining a level of an analyte of a user using an analyte
sensor, comprising:
storing, by processing circuitry, at least one parameter including a slope
associated with a sensitivity of the analyte sensor;
collecting, by the processing circuity, sensor data from the analyte sensor
when the analyte sensor is at least partially inserted into interstitial fluid of the user, the sensor data including data indicative of the level of the analyte in the
interstitial fluid;
obtaining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf start time from an electronic
memory communicatively coupled with the processing circuitry;
determining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf duration of the analyte
sensor based on the shelf start time;
determining, by the processing circuitry and based on the shelf duration,

an adjustment function of a plurality of adjustment functions configured to adjust processing of the sensor data, wherein each adjustment function of the plurality of adjustment functions differs from other adjustment functions of the plurality of
adjustment functions;
adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data using
the determined adjustment function to compensate for the shelf duration, the adjusting comprising adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the
analyte sensor;
determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the
user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope; and
outputting the determined level of the analyte to a display.
Even if the proposed Bohm-Hoss-Dobbles combination were proper, it would still fail to
disclose, teach, or suggest all of the limitations of independent claim 1.
As an example, the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination fails to disclose, teach, or suggest
"determining, by the processing circuitry and based on the shelf duration, an adjustment function
of a plurality of adjustment functions configured to adjust processing of the sensor data, wherein
each adjustment function of the plurality of adjustment functions differs from other adjustment
functions of the plurality of adjustment functions", as independent claim 1 recites. Bohm at most
describes conversion functions that change a slope with respect to the length of a sensor session.
As an example, FIGS. lA and 1B merely illustrate, and paragraph [0275] merely describes, a
plot of three conversion functions at different time periods within a sensor session. While FIG. 6
of Bohm illustrates an effect on sensitivity of the "time elapsed between sensor fabrication and
the start of the sensor session" (para. [0207]), Bohm merely describes a single curve as a function
of time (para. [0295]) and does not describe selecting from a plurality of different adjustment

functions "based on the shelf duration," such as based on the magnitude of the shelf duration. Any description in Bohm of modifying or varying a conversion function, which has been alleged to be similar or equivalent to the claimed adjustment function, with respect to time, merely describes changes in the conversion function based on the length of the sensor session, not the magnitude of the shelf duration. See, e.g., paras. [0269], [0343]. Consequently, the proposed Bohm-Hoss-Dobbles combination fails to disclose, teach, or suggest "determining, by the processing circuitry and based on the shelf duration, an adjustment function of a plurality of adjustment functions configured to adjust processing of the sensor data, wherein each adjustment function of the plurality of adjustment functions differs from other adjustment functions of the plurality of adjustment functions."

The Office may not disregard specific recitations of Applicant's claims to maintain a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103. According to the M.P.E.P., "[a]ll words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art." M.P.E.P. § 2143.03 (citations omitted). Moreover, "[w]hen evaluating claims for obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103, all the limitations of the claims must be considered and given weight." Id. (emphasis added). As shown above the proposed Bohm-Hoss-Dobbles combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all the limitations of independent claim 1. Therefore, the proposed Bohm-Hoss-Dobbles combination does not render independent claim 1 obvious.

For at least these reasons, independent claim 1 is allowable over the proposed Bohm- Hoss-Dobbles combination. Applicant respectfully requests the Office to reconsider and allow this independent claim and all its dependent claims.

Claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23, 25-28, and 74-76 depend, directly or indirectly, from independent claim 1. Applicant, therefore, respectfully submits that claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23, 25-28, and 74-76 are allowable at least based on their dependence from allowable independent claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23, 25-28, and 74-76 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be withdrawn.

Applicant submits that this application is in condition for allowance at least for the reasons set forth herein. If this application is not considered to be in condition for allowance by the Office, Applicant requests an interview with the Examiner to discuss this application. Applicant's Attorney Keith M. Jurek may be reached at telephone number (650) 739-7566 to schedule a mutually convenient date and time and to provide assistance or additional information as required.

Applicant submits that this Amendment and the accompanying remarks raise minimal new issues for consideration and do not necessitate the undertaking of an additional search of the art by the Office. This Amendment should therefore allow for immediate action by the Office.

On the basis of the foregoing remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the pending claims of this application are allowable over the art of record. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Office. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.

The above remarks are made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and do not constitute agreement with any reference identified or rejection raised by the Office Action. Applicant believes that a full and complete reply has been made to the outstanding Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Office. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.
